description: Filter VM 310 logs (and later VM 300, once Stage I-G installs its Alloy agent). Host and Job always exist as labels. Container exists only on Docker streams and unit only on journal streams, so they are applied with the extra Label filters control rather than AND-ed into every query. Retention is seven days; log history is disposable and is not part of the recovery plan.

links.tooltip: Raw LogQL editor, same Loki data source

panels.description: How the filters above this row combine. Label filters are optional; Host, Job, Severity, Match, and Exclude always apply.

options.content:
### How to filter

1. **Host** and **Job** — `docker` is container output, `journal` is systemd. Only hosts running Alloy appear (today: `observability` on VM 310).
2. **Label filters** (`+` next to the dropdowns) — add `container = grafana` or `unit = sshd.service`. Do not AND container and unit together; a stream has one or the other, never both.
3. **Severity** — presets that match on the text of the line. Loki has no `level` label here.
4. **Match** / **Exclude** — regular expressions against the line. Match is case-insensitive. Leave Match as `.*` and Exclude as `$^` to skip them.

Click a bar in **Top containers** or **Top systemd units** to jump to that source. Click a log line to expand its labels, then use *Filter for value*.

panels.description: Total number of log lines matching the current filters over the dashboard time range. If this is zero, the filters are too narrow: reset Match to .*, Severity to All, and clear Label filters before concluding that a service stopped logging.
panels.title: Matching lines

panels.description: Matching lines per five minutes, split by host and job. A sudden spike is usually a restart loop or a service that began logging an error on every request; a line that stops entirely means the source went away.
panels.title: Log volume

panels.description: The ten Docker containers producing the most matching lines. Click a bar to restrict Job to docker and add a container label filter. Journal records have no container label and are not in this panel.
panels.title: Top containers

panels.description: The ten systemd units producing the most matching lines. Click a bar to restrict Job to journal and add a unit label filter. Repeated session-NNN.scope entries are ordinary SSH logins, including this project's own automation.
panels.title: Top systemd units

panels.description: Matching log lines, newest first. Click a line to expand labels, then Filter for value to add a Label filter. This panel shows the same records the counters above are describing.
panels.title: Filtered log lines

list.description: Which machine the records came from. Only hosts running the Alloy agent appear here.
list.label: Host
list.name: host

list.description: docker is container stdout/stderr. journal is systemd. There is no syslog traffic yet.
list.label: Job
list.name: job

list.description: Optional extra matchers such as container=grafana or unit=sshd.service. Use + to add one. A Docker stream has container and a journal stream has unit; they are never on the same line.
list.label: Label filters
list.name: Filters

list.description: Severity presets applied as a case-insensitive line filter. Loki has no level label in this deployment, so these match on the text of the line itself.
list.label: Severity
list.name: sev
list.query: All : .*,Errors only : (?i)(error|fatal|critical|panic),Warnings and worse : (?i)(warn|error|fatal|critical|panic),Authentication and SSH : (?i)(sshd|authentication|invalid user|failed password|sudo),Service state changes : (?i)(started|stopped|restart|killed|oom)

list.description: Case-insensitive regular expression that a line must match. Leave as .* to match everything. Example: timeout|refused
list.label: Match (regex)
list.name: search

list.description: Regular expression for lines to drop. The default $^ matches nothing, so nothing is excluded. Example: session-[0-9]+
list.label: Exclude (regex)
list.name: exclude
